The bull case rests on the quarter ended 2026-07-31, when revenue reached $1.85 billion, up 36.54% from a year earlier, and net income reached $397 million, up 107.85% [D1]. Profitability improved with the top line, with a gross margin of 65.87% and a net margin of 21.51% [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group delivered revenue of $1.35 billion, up 43.09%, and operating income of $458 million, up 86.18%, while the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group delivered revenue of $501 million, up 21.60%, and operating income of $155 million, up 68.48% [D1]. Total segment operating income of $613 million was up 81.36% on the year [D1]. Management guided the fourth fiscal quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and to earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on 172 million diluted shares, growth of 37% at the mid-point of the revenue range [D1]. The beat was attributed to demand for testing linked to AI infrastructure, which lifted orders well above expectations [D2]. Management said commercial communications momentum continued into the second half and that wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3]. For the bull case to hold, the next report needs revenue at or above $1.93 billion and earnings per share at or above $3.34, the bottom of the guided ranges [D1].

The bear case starts with the market's reaction, a fall of 6.32% in the session of 2026-08-19 that followed the 2026-08-18 release [D2]. The prior release on 2026-05-19 was followed by a decline of 0.59% in the session of 2026-05-20 [D2]. Even after the beat, the shares still carry a trailing price to earnings ratio of 45.89 against a forward price to earnings ratio of 20.66, so the growth is already discounted [D5]. Management described the supply environment as less flexible than a year ago and said the supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue, with the supply situation likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also cautioned that the one-time tariff impacts this year will not repeat, which raises the comparison bar for future profitability [D3]. Analysts pressed on whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints, rather than demand, capped the guidance [D3]. For the bear case to hold, the next report needs revenue below $1.93 billion or earnings per share below $3.34 [D1], together with confirmation that supply remains the binding constraint on converting demand into revenue [D3].
